word:greek-nt:G0017.explanation: This word means “doing good” and can describe “one who does good.” It points to good action, whether emphasizing the action itself or the person carrying it out. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Peter 2:14. The word’s basic sense is clear, while the precise role it plays in that verse depends on the surrounding sentence and passage.

word:greek-nt:G0080.explanation: Adelphos means brother. It can also refer to a member of the same religious community.

word:greek-nt:G0163.explanation: Aichmalōtizō means to take captive, whether people are led away captive or thoughts are brought into captivity.

word:greek-nt:G0189.explanation: Akoē means hearing, the faculty of hearing. It can also mean a report. It can also mean a rumor.

word:greek-nt:G0219.explanation: Alektorophōnia means the cockcrow, the time marked by a rooster’s crowing.

word:greek-nt:G0633.explanation: Aponipto means to wash dirt off.

word:greek-nt:G0695.explanation: This word means “silversmith,” a person who makes or works with objects made of silver. It functions as a noun, naming someone by his occupation rather than describing an action or quality. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 19:24. The word itself identifies the trade; the surrounding verse and passage determine what this particular silversmith was doing or why he is mentioned.

word:greek-nt:G0718.explanation: Harmozo means to betroth or promise someone in marriage.

word:greek-nt:G0754.explanation: This word refers to a chief tax collector—a person who held a leading role in collecting taxes. It identifies the person’s occupation and position rather than describing an action or feeling. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Luke 19:2. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself directly names a tax collector with chief responsibility or rank.

word:greek-nt:G0875.explanation: Aphrizō means to foam or froth, including at the mouth.

word:greek-nt:G0956.explanation: This word means “arrow” or “arrows,” referring to a projectile shot through the air. It is a concrete noun that names the object itself, not the act of shooting or the person who uses it. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Ephesians 6:16. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding verse text and context, but its ordinary meaning remains the same: an arrow, or arrows considered as a group. The word therefore provides a straightforward picture of a weapon used against a target.

word:greek-nt:G0981.explanation: This word refers to a person’s lifestyle—the way that person lives. It describes life as a continuing pattern or manner of living, rather than a single action. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 26:4, so its precise emphasis there depends on the surrounding verse and passage. Its basic sense is a person’s established way of life or daily conduct.

word:greek-nt:G1010.explanation: Bouleutēs means a member of a city council. Joseph is described as a member of the council.

word:greek-nt:G1087.explanation: Gerousia means an assembly or body of elders.

word:greek-nt:G1252.explanation: Diakrino means to distinguish or discern one thing from another. It can also mean to doubt or waver.

word:greek-nt:G1304.explanation: Diatribō means to stay in a place. It can also describe tarrying or continuing there: Jesus tarried with his disciples, and Paul and Barnabas continued in Antioch.

word:greek-nt:G1348.explanation: Dikastēs means a judge, someone who holds judicial authority.

word:greek-nt:G1371.explanation: Dichotomeō means to cut in two or cut to pieces.

word:greek-nt:G1425.explanation: This Greek New Testament word means “hard to understand.” It describes something difficult to grasp clearly, whether because the idea is complex or requires careful thought. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, at 2 Peter 3:16. Its basic sense identifies difficulty in understanding rather than declaring that something is impossible to understand; the surrounding passage determines the particular matter being described. [p03:word:greek-nt:G1425:identity] [p01:word:greek-nt:G1425:reference:0] [p03:word:greek-nt:G1425:occurrences]

word:greek-nt:G1469.explanation: This word means “to classify”: to place someone or something into a considered category or assessment. It describes an act of judging or sorting rather than merely noticing. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 2 Corinthians 10:12. Its precise force in that passage depends on the surrounding verse and argument, but its basic meaning is the act of making a classification or assessment.

word:greek-nt:G1483.explanation: This word means “Gentile-like” or “like a Gentile.” It describes conduct or manner that resembles that of a Gentile, rather than naming a person directly. Its meaning is concerned with how someone acts or presents himself. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Galatians 2:14. The surrounding verse is needed to explain the particular force of the word there, but its basic sense is behavior that is Gentile-like.

word:greek-nt:G1537.explanation: Ek means from, out of, or out from among, suggesting movement from the interior outward. It can also mark origin, as in being from men or from among brothers.

word:greek-nt:G1692.explanation: “To spit out” or “to vomit” means to expel something from the mouth or stomach. This Greek New Testament verb pictures forceful rejection, not merely speaking or allowing something to fall away. It occurs once in the Greek New Testament, at Revelation 3:16. The precise force of the word in that verse depends on its surrounding sentence and passage, but the word itself plainly describes something being expelled.

word:greek-nt:G1788.explanation: Entrepo means to put to shame or cause shame. It can also mean to reverence or regard someone.

word:greek-nt:G1832.explanation: Exestin means that something is permitted or lawful.

word:greek-nt:G1924.explanation: Epigrapho means to write upon, inscribe, or imprint a mark on.

word:greek-nt:G1951.explanation: This word expresses being “called” or “chosen,” and can describe the act of calling or choosing someone. It functions as a word about designation—someone being called by a particular name or selected for a purpose. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, in John 5:2 and Acts 15:40. Its precise force in either verse depends on the surrounding sentence and passage, but its central idea remains calling or choosing.

word:greek-nt:G1968.explanation: Epipiptō means to fall upon or press upon. It describes people pressing upon someone so they could touch him.

word:greek-nt:G2099.explanation: Euangelistēs means an evangelist—a missionary who bears good tidings. Philip is called an evangelist, and the work of an evangelist is presented as a task to perform.

word:greek-nt:G2136.explanation: Euodia is the personal name of a person mentioned in the Greek New Testament. It is rendered “Euodia,” and it occurs once, in Philippians 4:2. As a name, it identifies an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general concept. The word itself does not provide a wider definition beyond that personal designation. Its precise role in the verse depends on the surrounding passage, while its lexical contribution remains the person’s name.

word:greek-nt:G2194.explanation: Zaboulōn is the name Zebulun, also used for the tribe of Zebulun.

word:greek-nt:G2460.explanation: Hippeus means a horse-soldier, or mounted soldier.

word:greek-nt:G2529.explanation: This Greek New Testament verb means “to be clearly seen,” “to have been perceived,” or “to perceive.” It describes something that can be recognized plainly rather than remaining hidden or indistinct. The word focuses on clear perception—seeing or understanding something sufficiently for it to be noticed. It occurs once in the Greek New Testament, in Romans 1:20, so its precise force there belongs to the surrounding verse and passage.

word:greek-nt:G2565.explanation: Kallielaios means a cultivated olive tree.

word:greek-nt:G2662.explanation: Katapateō means to trample down or under foot.

word:greek-nt:G2767.explanation: Kerannymi means to mix or mingle.

word:greek-nt:G2903.explanation: This word describes someone or something as “excellent” or “most excellent.” It expresses a high degree of distinction or quality and can function as a respectful description of a person. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs four times, all in Luke and Acts. Its use in formal address shows that it can identify someone viewed as especially distinguished. The exact force in a particular verse depends on the surrounding wording and situation.

word:greek-nt:G3009.explanation: Leitourgia means service or ministry. It can also describe service carried out by giving to meet a need among fellow believers.

word:greek-nt:G3100.explanation: Mathēteuō means to make disciples, training people in discipleship. It can also describe being trained or instructed as a disciple.

word:greek-nt:G3197.explanation: Melchi is the name of one of Jesus’ ancestors.

word:greek-nt:G3328.explanation: Metaballō means to change. It can also mean to change one's mind. For example, people changed their minds after seeing no harm come to him.

word:greek-nt:G3423.explanation: This word means “to be pledged to marriage” or “to betroth.” It describes the relationship or action connected with a marriage commitment made before the wedding itself. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs three times, all in Matthew and Luke, in references concerning Mary and Joseph’s relationship. The word therefore points to a recognized promise or commitment to marry, rather than simply a general association between a man and woman. Its precise force in any particular verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:greek-nt:G3485.explanation: Naos means a temple or shrine.

word:greek-nt:G3557.explanation: Nosphizō means to hold back part of something for oneself. It can also mean to purloin.

word:greek-nt:G3676.explanation: Homōs means yet or nevertheless. It can also mean even, adding an additional case.

word:greek-nt:G3715.explanation: Lust is a word for strong, uncontrolled sexual desire. It names an inward craving rather than a mere physical action, so it describes what a person wants or desires. In the Greek New Testament, this word occurs once, in Romans 1:27. The English rendering is “lust,” matching its central meaning. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, which is not included here.

word:greek-nt:G3759.explanation: Ouai means “woe” or “alas,” an expression of grief or denunciation. It appears in warnings addressed to cities and to scribes and Pharisees.

word:greek-nt:G3922.explanation: Pareiserchomai means to come in or enter. It can also describe entering secretly.

word:greek-nt:G4123.explanation: Pleonektēs means a covetous or greedy person, one desirous of having more.

word:greek-nt:G4185.explanation: Polytelēs means very costly, precious, or of great value.

word:greek-nt:G4215.explanation: Potamos means a river or stream.

word:greek-nt:G4398.explanation: Prophetess means a woman who is a prophet.

word:greek-nt:G4400.explanation: Procheirizo means to appoint or choose.

word:greek-nt:G4497.explanation: Rhoboam is the personal name Rehoboam.

word:greek-nt:G4509.explanation: Rhypos means filth, dirt, or squalor.

word:greek-nt:G4545.explanation: Samuel is the name of a Hebrew prophet.

word:greek-nt:G4611.explanation: Siloam is the name of a water source.

word:greek-nt:G4628.explanation: Skelos means the leg, the part of the body from the hip downward.

word:greek-nt:G4664.explanation: This word means “emerald,” the name of a precious green stone. It names the gemstone itself rather than an action, quality, or person. It occurs once in the Greek New Testament, at Revelation 4:3. Because the verse text and surrounding passage are not included here, the word’s precise descriptive role in that verse must be understood from its context. Its central meaning remains the gemstone called an emerald.

word:greek-nt:G4826.explanation: Symeon is a personal name rendered Simeon or Simon.

word:greek-nt:G4884.explanation: Synarpazō means to seize or drag by force.

word:greek-nt:G5050.explanation: Teleiōsis means completion or fulfillment. It can also mean perfection.

word:greek-nt:G5102.explanation: This word means a “sign” or “title”—a written designation that identifies someone or states who they are. It can refer to a notice placed where others can read it, or to the title assigned to a person. In the Greek New Testament, it appears twice, both times in John 19. Its precise force in either occurrence is clarified by the surrounding passage, but its central idea is a written identifying designation.

word:greek-nt:G5256.explanation: Hypēreteō means to minister to or serve.

word:greek-nt:G5281.explanation: Hypomonē means endurance, steadfastness, or patient waiting. It can describe perseverance in well-doing.

word:greek-nt:G5339.explanation: Pheidomai means to spare. It can also mean to refrain or forbear, holding back from an action.

word:greek-nt:G5375.explanation: Philippi is the name of a city in Macedonia.

word:greek-nt:G5506.explanation: Chiliarchos means a military officer, especially a commander of a thousand men.
